updates.alert: I'm making no trades this week. All 13 positions were bought on October 19, and nothing in the data breaks any thesis. CrowdStrike (+13%) and Fortinet (+5%) got the security-software rebound I was hoping for. The refiners (Marathon -3.8%, Valero -3.3%) gave back some of their gains after a strong month, which is normal ahead of their third-quarter reports. My two weak spots are Keysight, which is down 6% and sitting right on its 200-day average, and Morgan Stanley, which is below its 200-day average and 21% under its high. I'm watching both, but swapping them five days after buying would cost commissions and taxes for no clear edge. The main risks are refiner and Merck earnings, energy being about 23% of the portfolio, a deeper slide in Keysight, and whether this week's software rebound holds.
updates.market_view: The S&P 500 was flat this week (-0.2%) and is slightly down over the month, but 56% of members are still above their 200-day averages, so the market is drifting rather than breaking down. Money keeps moving toward defensives and real-asset sectors: Utilities, Energy, Staples and Health Care led over the past month. Last cycle's AI hardware leaders (chip equipment, storage, optical) are still falling hard. Security software bounced sharply this week.
updates.self_review: Wednesday's decision to hold and not chase chip equipment and storage was right: Lam (-13%) and KLA (-12%) kept falling this week, while our security-software names rebounded. The portfolio is up about 1.4% since inception against a flat S&P 500.

updates.alert: I'm leaving the portfolio as it is. These 13 positions were bought only two days ago, and nothing in this week's data breaks any thesis. The positions are up between -1.5% and +8.4%. The only trade will be a small trim of Merck to bring it back under the 10% cap, because its gains pushed it to 10.1%. I looked at the deep dips in chip equipment and storage (Lam, Applied Materials, Western Digital, Seagate), but they are still falling and below their 200-day averages, so buying now would be trying to catch the bottom. Switching into them would also cost commissions for no clear edge. The main risks I'm watching are the refiners' third-quarter reports (Marathon, Valero), Merck's earnings and pipeline update, further selling in security software, and Morgan Stanley, which is my weakest holding and below its 200-day average.
updates.market_view: The S&P 500 is flat over the month and up 4.7% over three months, and 55% of members are above their 200-day average, so the market is holding up but not broadly strong. Leadership has moved to energy, health care and consumer staples. AI hardware and semiconductors keep correcting: many of last year's winners now sit 25-50% below their highs. Third-quarter earnings season is the main catalyst over the next two weeks.

updates.alert: This is the first decision, so I'm putting about 90% of the $10,000 into 13 stocks and holding 10% in cash. The biggest positions are Merck, Marathon Petroleum, Targa Resources and Nucor. Each has strong 12-month gains and kept rising or held steady this week while the rest of the market fell. I'm buying cybersecurity (CrowdStrike, Fortinet) and storage (NetApp) after their 13-17% drops this week. Their trends are intact, and buying now means entering below their recent highs. I'm deliberately skipping the most extreme momentum names, Moderna (+732% in 12 months), Lumentum and Bloom Energy, because their daily price swings are too wild to size sensibly. The main risks I'm watching: refining margins could fall back, the AI and tech selling could spread to my software names, and a broader pullback could hit Morgan Stanley through weaker capital-markets activity. These are judgments from the brief's price data only; I didn't run any news searches this week.
updates.market_view: The S&P 500 fell 2.1% this week and is flat over the last month. Only about half its members trade above their 200-day average, so the market's strength is narrow. This week's selling hit the AI and hardware names hard: Lumentum, Dell, HPE and Coherent each fell 20-25%. Leadership has moved to energy, especially refiners, and to health care, while communication services keep falling. I'm building a diversified portfolio weighted toward steadier momentum: refiners, pipelines, pharma, steel and cybersecurity. I'm keeping 10% cash because the market is fragile.

new.thesis: Large pharma with +74% 12-1 month momentum, low volatility and a strong balance sheet. Health care is the best defensive sector this quarter (+12.5% over 3 months).
Leading refiner trading only 1% under its 52-week high, up 13% this month and 49% over 3 months as refining margins widen. Large share buybacks support the stock.

A second refiner that benefits from the same margin conditions, with steady operations and strong cash returns to shareholders. I'm holding it smaller than MPC to limit how much I depend on one industry.
Pipeline company earning fee-based income from growing natural-gas volumes. It has near-high momentum (+91% 12-1 month) with only moderate volatility.
Steelmaker with +93% 12-1 month momentum and low volatility for its sector, helped by tariff protection and a conservative balance sheet.
Leader in endpoint security with growing recurring revenue. After this week's 17% drop it is a chance to buy a strong +102% 12-1 month trend that is still well above its 200-day average.
Security company with good profitability and a firewall upgrade cycle, now 13% under its high after this week's drop.
Storage company with a cheaper valuation than other AI hardware, benefiting from demand for flash storage in data centers. It is +23% over 3 months even after this week's pullback.
Test-and-measurement company with improving orders across AI, wireless and defense customers, and +104% 12-1 month momentum.
Leader in gene sequencing whose results are recovering. The stock is +36% over 3 months and 54% above its 200-day average.
Cheap generic-drug maker at a fresh 52-week high, with debt coming down and cash going back to shareholders.
DuPont after its split, now a more focused company in electronics and water. The stock is up 69% in 12 months and has moved only modestly in the past month, a calm way to own industrial exposure.
Wealth-management franchise whose stock is 21% off its high. I'm making it a small position to add financials at a lower price.
